subject: kernel values for females and males

messages.author: 2734d59aee5d72a5
messages.subject: kernel values for females and males
parts:
Hi all,

I am running open pop spatially explicit models, using JSSAsecrlCL with openCR package, for seven ocelot surveys. The best fitted model, according to AICc, has the following parameters:
 
lambda0~Sex, phi~Sex, l~1, sigma~Sex, move.a~Sex

Move.a parameter is really different for females and for males.
To report the kernel values, I am using the function "make.kernel", but the values I get back are values for females only. How can I extract the values for males? Any idea?
Thank you very much
Best
Paula

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: kernel values for females and males
parts:
make.kernel() can be used with various inputs. You are applying it to an existing openCR model, in which case make.kernel internally calls predict.openCR(movementmodel,...) to determine the parameter(s) of the kernel. You should be able to pass covariates with the dots argument:
kF <- make.kernel(fit, newdata = data.frame(session = 1, Sex = 'F'))
kM <- make.kernel(fit, newdata = data.frame(session = 1, Sex = 'M'))
But I haven't tested this.

If that fails, you can simply call make.kernel with appropriate values
make.kernel(movementmodel = 'BVE', move.a = X, ...)
where X is the value for females or males from predict(fit) and ... includes other named arguments as specified (or default) in your original model.
Murray
